text: Backups tab, Back up mode: the Scriptmix "Duplicate Current Layer" (Scripts/Masters/). Clone master layers of the selected glyphs into " backup " layers. The backup naming is the App's shared rule ( masters.inspect.model.backup_master / backup_layer_name , custom suffixes, legacy @ and overlapping names, exact-case prefixes, casefolded master names refused), reused, not copied. The table lists each new backup, special layers kept and the existing backups (the original panel's inventory). Back up writes every clone as ONE Layer Manager: back up <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history with no target layers (the original's layer-creating layers=[] route); the new layers are not master and not automatic layers ( isMasterLayer / autoLayer stay False).
title: fontlabapp.studios.layer_manager._duplicate

text: Deliver tab, mode "Copy layers from font": the Examples "Copy Layers From Font" (Scripts/Tools/). The current font is the destination; the source font is chosen from the open fonts. Map source and destination layer names, choose a collision mode, press Preview, inspect the kept rows, confirm, then Copy. Copy re-surveys both fonts and refuses a plan that differs from the Preview ("Source or destination changed; Preview again."), then writes ONE Layer Manager: copy layers from font <subject> Undo step in the destination through AppShell.history with the destination window guards ( window= ). The source is only read. The name checks, font resolution, capture, survey and clone repair are the original's, verbatim. Native cross-font Undo and Redo are not qualified here (Scriptmix TODO, T29).

text: Pieces every Layer Manager tab shares: backends, the Undo label, one write route, the plan tab. What: backends() returns core.scripting.layer_manager_backends() (tests replace it); Modules lets the verbatim originals keep reading their module names. label builds "Layer Manager: <action> <subject>" . commit is the one write route of the tabs: tool.shell.history over explicit live layers (None when refused; the shell status says why). PlanTab is the host-mode form of the originals' panels: the tab's controls, a sortable GlyphTable dry run (a row choice shows that glyph and layer in the TGlyph preview), a status line, "Use selection" (rebinds the tab to the current font and its Font-window selection, as the originals' button and their open did) and one explicit verb button. Apply plans again from the bound font and refuses a plan that differs from the list on screen ( STALE ), then writes. Used by fontlabapp.studios.layer_manager .

text: Backups tab, Use as master mode: the Scriptmix "Use Layer As Master" (Scripts/Masters/). Swap the roles of a chosen layer and the master layer it belongs to by renaming only: the old master layer becomes " @ HH:MM:SS, DD/MM/YY", the chosen layer takes the master name, and their masks follow FontLab's mask-name rule. The naming and swap planning ( mask_name_for , plan_swap , _mask_of ) are the original's, verbatim, and every original refusal is kept. Host-mode deviation (disclosed): the original promoted the layer selected in a Glyph window; here the tab lists the selected glyphs' layers that belong to a master but are not its master layer, and the "Layer" choice names the layer to promote. Use as master writes all renames as ONE Layer Manager: use as master <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history (names put back on failure, as the original did).

text: Clean-up tab: the Scriptmix "Layer Cleanup" (Scripts/Masters/) and "Empty Layers" (Scripts/Cleanup/). Mode "Delete ticked" (Layer Cleanup): list the extra layers (masks, backups, alternates, others) of the selected glyphs; nothing is ticked at first; the "Tick" buttons tick every free row of a kind, or none; "Tick row" toggles the chosen row (the shared GlyphTable has no tick boxes, so the "Ticked" column shows the ticks; disclosed). Shown, locked and refused layers are listed as kept and cannot be ticked. "Delete Ticked" plans again and refuses ticks that no longer match ("The layers changed. Check the table and tick again."). Mode "Empty layers" (Empty Layers): list the extra layers that hold no data, then delete them. The planning is the originals', verbatim. Each delete is ONE Layer Manager: ... Undo step through AppShell.history on the originals' carrier layers; the components of deleted layers are retained (fl#7641); layers go by the originals' glyph.removeLayer route.

text: Copy between masters tab: the Scriptmix "Copy Layer Between Masters" (Scripts/Masters/). For each selected glyph, replace the contours of the checked target master layers with repaired clones of the source master's contours; optionally move same-named anchors to the source positions and set the source advance width. Components of the targets stay. The planning functions are the original's, verbatim: auto layers, glyphs refused by the auto-glyph facts, locked layers, metrics links or expressions, a source without outline, duplicated anchor names and anchors that would move to 0, 0 (fl#8527) are listed and skipped. Copy plans again, refuses a plan that differs from the list, and writes every target layer as one Layer Manager: copy layers <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history , then reads contours, widths and anchors back.

text: Deliver tab: the Scriptmix "Deliver Glyphs" (Scripts/Masters/) and the Examples "Copy Layers From Font". Mode "Deliver glyphs": the source glyphs are captured when the tab opens or on "Use selection as source" (never on a refresh: the original bound its source when it opened). Activate the destination Font window, press Preview, check the rows, then Deliver. Missing glyphs are added with FontLab's Add Glyph ( glyphs.creation : one Undo step per new glyph, the original's route), then every eligible master layer is filled as ONE Layer Manager: deliver glyphs <subject> Undo step through AppShell.history . Only the destination font is written. The planning, master pairing and the Delivery editor are the original's, verbatim; Deliver refuses a destination or plan that differs from the Preview ("The delivery changed; click Preview again."). Native cross-font Undo and Redo are not qualified here (Scriptmix TODO, T29). Mode "Copy layers from font": _from_font .

text: Cursive tab (Scriptmix Auto Cursive Attachment Get Sample and Add Anchors). Get sample: one selected body layer with entry / exit anchors inside closed ink is measured ( measure_sample ) and saved as a NEW fontlab-cursive-sample-1 JSON file (an existing file is never overwritten; default folder: home). The format is the originals', so the old and the new tool read each other's samples. It writes nothing to the font. Add anchors: the sample (same master only) fits the missing exit (ini, med) and entry (fin, med) anchors of the selected glyphs on the current master: 10–500 unit ink spans near the connection edge, scored by thickness and boundary angle, rounded half up ( choose_attachment , cursive_changes ; unchanged). A layer that cannot be fitted becomes a note row. Apply writes the listed anchors as one Mark Attachment: add cursive anchors <subject> Undo step. The originals import fly.ap.anchors.writer inside two functions; here that name is the reused backend ( anchor_writer below), the only change.

text: The Outline Doctor check registry: one Check per absorbed Scriptmix script. What: CHECKS lists the fourteen checks in tab order with their options, thresholds and default master scope exactly as the scripts had them. Structural fixes (they add or remove nodes or contours) default to All masters with Keep masters compatible ticked; Retract Handles and Round Coordinates default to the current master; Curve All Straights and Straighten All Curves default to All masters; the three reports are read-only. Why: session and tabs look checks up here; by_key and in_tab are the only lookups.

text: Outline Doctor read-only reports: Open Contours, Close But No Cigar, Dangerous Offcurves. What: three planners that return Issue rows with no edit. Open Contours lists every open contour with its node count and end gap; Close But No Cigar (after Simon Cozens' glyphmonkey script, MIT) lists angles within 2° of horizontal or vertical, segment lengths within 5 % of a master stem and nodes within 2 units of zero or a vertical metric; Dangerous Offcurves lists cubic handles closer than 0.05 units to their own curve on all four axis probes. Why: they are the Scan tab's whole-font and selection reports; they never write.

What: Doctor reuses the Transform Studio session for fonts, masters, glyph lookup and hint removal, and adds scan (read-only: never opens a history step), plan (with the compatibility guard of the Scriptmix outline panel), ghost (the planned after-outline over the TGlyph preview, with the affected points highlighted) and fix (one AppShell.history step named "Outline Doctor: <action> <subject>" on the explicit layers, then the check's own read-back). Why: every checks.Check runs through the same guarded path. Layers with PostScript hints are refused unless the caller opts in.

text: Proof Studio generator registry: one module per generator, listed per tab. What: every non-underscore module in this package defines GENERATOR , a Generator . generators() imports them (sorted by tab order, then the generator's order ) and tab_titles() lists the tabs they name. A new tab or generator is a new module only; nothing here changes. Why: Phase D A7 absorbs 26 Scriptmix proof scripts in two tasks; T9 adds Real text, Random, Word finder, Waterfall and By master as further modules. Contract: make(choice, options) is pure (no Qt, no host, no writes) and returns a Proof . open(choice) opens the new FontLab Glyph tab(s) exactly as the absorbed script did; it never edits the font. Persistence is limited to the absorbed tool's own QSettings namespace ( settings ). Used by fontlabapp.studios.proof_studio (tab registration, tabs and session).

text: Proof Studio state: selection and font facts, generation, preview, copy, open and actions. What: Studio turns the chosen generator, choice, seed and field values into a Proof , previews a part through TMetrics ( set_view for size and kerning, set_layer for the master, then set_text ), hands the exact part text to a clipboard callable, draws Waterfall and By master stacks in the absorbed panels' own views ( paint ), opens the FontLab Glyph tab(s) through the generator and runs generator actions. Every preview sets size, layer and kerning, so one tab's settings never leak into another's. Read-only for font data: it never edits the font, never calls history and reads the selection or font facts only when the generator uses them. Its only writes are a generator's own settings namespace. Qt-free. Used by fontlabapp.studios.proof_studio (app and tabs).

text: Proof Studio tab panel: generator, choice, part and seed pickers, fields, preview, copy and open. What: one GeneratorTab per registry tab (Pattern strings, Kerning proofs, Real text, Random, Word finder, Waterfall, By master). Each generator gets a page of its own fields and action buttons; changing the generator, choice, part, seed or a field regenerates the proof and previews it in TMetrics (contract §1.8). The read-only text box shows the exact text that Copy puts on the clipboard; a report box shows action reports (coverage JSON). "Open in FontLab Glyph tab" runs the absorbed script's backend. A generator with a settings namespace loads from it at build and saves after user edits (or on its explicit Save action). Nothing here writes to the font. text: Split ribbon contours into evenly spaced strips. What: Split ribbon contours into evenly spaced strips. How: The shortest opposing compatible line segments form caps. Pair the intervening edges in opposite directions and interpolate their coordinates. Equal segment types are required. New contours replace the ribbon. Read-back allows 0.5 unit per axis for native rounding. Why: Make a striped outline while retaining cubic edge geometry. Use: Set strip count and filled percentage. Inspect the contour counts, then Apply. Benefit: Generates editable strips over selected glyphs and masters. Rebuilt contours have new node identities. The non-modal panel previews the selected glyphs and chosen masters. Shared, scaled and rotated outline shapes are kept. Automatic-layer owners are kept. Bases of automatic composites are kept unless the shared consent option is enabled. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step through the App history writer. Reload after changing the selection. Independent behaviour rewrite after Simon Cozens, GlyphsScripts/Comb.py, MIT, copyright 2017 Simon Cozens. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No source code was copied.

text: Generate width-fitted Myanmar medial-ra variants on every FontLab master. What: Group consonants on the current master. Fit the same group members on all masters, using each master's mean advance minus its own template enclosure. Names use the current master's group means floored to tens. Also create eight unstretched omission variants. Existing names and targets with a bad master are kept, with the master and reason listed. How: Read U+1000–U+1020 by Unicode or hexadecimal name. Verify the five pieces: stem, top rail, top hook, bottom rail, bottom hook. The stem must be tallest; top pieces above bottom pieces; hooks right of rails. The rails' closing edges must be on their right, the hooks' on their left. Copy through the shared App contour copier. Show every target's extension and node/handle bounds on every master in the Preview table. Apply refuses source data changed since Preview. Why: Fit this five-part Myanmar outline to consonant width groups. All-master output keeps the generated glyph structure consistent across masters; a failed template keeps the entire target. Use: Select one template, or leave the selection empty to use U+103C. Inspect Preview and consent to any listed automatic-glyph rebuilds, then Apply. Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step. Benefit: Produce a compatible set of fitted medial-ra variants for refinement. Credit: Independent behaviour-only rewrite of Simon Cozens, GlyphsScripts/Myanmar Medial Ra Maker.py, MIT, copyright 2017. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No source code copied.

text: Construct geometric sans capitals in empty selected master layers. What: Build A, E, F, H, I, L, N, O, S, T, V, X, Y and Z from explicit height, width, vertical stroke, horizontal stroke and side space dimensions. How: Compose rectangles, diagonal strips, an elliptical ring or a cubic S. Union the filled pieces with Qt, then use the shared contour converter and outline writer. Existing outlines, components, locked layers and linked metrics are kept and named in the preview. No glyph or layer is created. Why: FontLab's Rectangle and Ellipse tools draw individual pieces. This panel constructs complete letter skeletons across selected glyphs and masters. Explicit dimensions replace the Glyphs Dimension palette; no host callbacks are installed. Use: Select empty capital glyphs in the Font window. Set the five dimensions, inspect the non-modal preview and choose current or all masters. Press Build. To give each master its own dimensions, untick Keep masters compatible, choose Current master, and set that master's dimensions before Build. Each changing action is recorded as one Undo step. Clear an outline with native FontLab tools before building that glyph again. Unsupported capitals are kept. Benefit: Start a consistent geometric alphabet without overwriting existing work. Diagonal ends are horizontal at the baseline and cap height. S spans both levels. The common dimensions are a construction model; per-letter source sliders and the source's continuous destructive redraw are replaced by explicit Build. Independent behaviour rewrite after Simon Cozens, Sansomatic.py, MIT. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No source code copied.

text: Spacing Studio arithmetic: sidebearing plans, offsets, comparisons and base-first order. What: Qt-free functions over whole font units. Metrics is one layer's measured state; each rule ( tuned , equalized , centred , copied , synced , italic ) returns the new left and right sidebearings (and width) that make_plan turns into a Plan : the outline shift dx and the new advance. order_plans puts bases before composites per master and removes the plan of any composite whose base moves in the same step, so no outline is moved twice (App TODO:37, Scriptmix TODO:74). Why: The maths of the nine absorbed Scriptmix metrics scripts and the Layer Metric Comparison example, kept testable without FontLab. Used by fontlabapp.studios.spacing_studio.session and .tabs .
title: fontlabapp.studios.spacing_studio.model

text: Spacing Studio state: native layer reads, base-first plans and one-step writes. What: Studio keeps the glyph list, the preview master and the last plan. plan reads each named glyph's explicit layer on the chosen masters ( flGlyph.findLayer ; never a glyph-level pen or fgGlyph ), skips missing, auto, metrics-linked and hinted layers with a note, and orders bases before composites, dropping a composite whose base moves ( model.order_plans ). apply writes every pending layer through AppShell.history as one "Spacing Studio: <action> <subject>" Undo step on those explicit layers, then reads each layer back. Why: Contract §1.3/§1.4 and App TODO:37/Scriptmix TODO:74 (no double shift). Hinted layers stay refused until the user runs "Remove PostScript hints", the shared Issue 241 remover ( fontui.remove_hints ), one Undo step per layer. Used by fontlabapp.studios.spacing_studio.tabs .

text: Qt-free outline snapshots, affine maths, edit simulation and the ghost overlay. What: Layer / Shape / Contour / Node are read-only snapshots of one native layer ( native.snapshot ). Planners turn a snapshot into Change rows whose edit is a tuple of steps: ("shape", shape, matrix, bake) sets a shape transform; bake folds it into the nodes (own outlines), otherwise it stays (components). ("node", shape, contour, node, x, y, smooth) moves one node (shape-local coordinates; smooth None keeps it). ("remove", shape, contour, indices, count) deletes nodes. ("anchor", index, x, y) and ("advance", width) . simulate applies steps to a snapshot and ghost draws the result as a TGlyph overlay; verify compares a read-back snapshot with the plan. Why: the Studio boundary forbids importing fontlabapp.contours ; this module privately repeats its affine contract ( a, b, c, d, e, f = QTransform(m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy) ). Shared by Transform Studio and Align & Nudge ( fontlabapp.studios.align_nudge ).

text: Read one native FontLab layer into a geometry.Layer and write planned steps back. What: snapshot(layer) copies shapes, contours, nodes (position, on-curve, smooth, selection), anchors and the advance into plain tuples, retaining no native wrapper. write(layer, steps) performs the steps inside the caller's history scope: shape transforms through QTransform (baked with applyTransform for own outlines), node moves, node removal, anchor points and the advance. shape.changed() follows every shape edit. Why: the planners stay Qt-free; this is the only module that touches native objects. Writes target the explicit layer a session resolved with flGlyph.findLayer ; never fgGlyph .

text: Studio state shared by Transform Studio and Align & Nudge: reads, plans, ghost and one-step writes. What: Studio keeps the glyph list, the preview master and the last plan. plan reads each named glyph's explicit layer on the chosen masters ( flGlyph.findLayer ; never fgGlyph ), snapshots it with native.snapshot and runs planner(name, master, snapshot) . Missing, auto, planner-noted and hinted layers are skipped with a note; hinted layers are written only when the user ticks "Edit hinted layers anyway" or runs "Remove PostScript hints" ( fontui.remove_hints ). ghost simulates the plan for the preview glyph and draws it with preview.set_overlay . apply writes every pending layer through AppShell.history as one "<App>: <action> <subject>" Undo step on those explicit layers, then reads every layer back with geometry.verify ; a difference is reported as "Partly applied", never as success. Why: Contract §1.3/§1.4. Read-only paths ( plan , ghost ) never open history. APP is a class attribute so fontlabapp.studios.align_nudge reuses this class with its own name and labels.

text: The three Transform Studio tabs (Transform, Slant, Rotate & reflect) and the shared Tab base. What: each tab is a plain Qt widget over the shared Studio state with the same glyph row (names field, "Use font selection", preview master, "All masters", the bases opt-in where the original script offered it) and a sortable GlyphTable of the last plan: one row per change, or one row per skipped layer with its note. Choosing a row shows that glyph in the TGlyph preview. Every action has a "Preview" button that plans, fills the table and draws the planned outline as a ghost ( preview.set_overlay ) without writing, and an apply button that writes one labelled Undo step. Hinted layers are skipped unless "Edit hinted layers anyway" is ticked or their hints are removed. Why: one window replaces six Scriptmix Scripts/Contours tools (Phase D A6). Tab and the field helpers are reused by fontlabapp.studios.align_nudge.tabs .

text: Calculate tab: Calculate Vertical Metrics (Font Info) and Vertical Metrics Reporter (Reports). Calculate: Refresh measures the bounds of every nonempty glyph in every master ( scan_bounds , the original 2.5 s interactive deadline) and the dry run lists, per master in scope, the font-info fields that would enclose every glyph, rounded outward ( enclosing_metrics ): padding 0–2000 and line gap 0–32767 (both default 0); the hhea and Win groups are ticked, the OS/2 Typo group (= FontLab's own ascender, descender and line gap) is optional and off, as in the original. "Set metrics" writes exactly the listed plan through the original writer core.scripting.write_font_info (it refuses a value that changed since the preview) as one Vertical Metrics: calculate metrics of <masters> Undo step. Bounds are captured on Refresh; press Refresh after outline edits. The glyph list keeps the original glyph_records read (legacy FL.fl.font order and fgGlyph.unicodes ); moving it to the shared studios._records catalogue waits for the native check (Scriptmix TODO:48, T10 ruling, T29) and is disclosed in the task report. Reporter: "Compare open fonts" reads eight stored metrics of every master in every open font ( metrics.vertical.native.capture ) and shows the original text report ( metrics.vertical.model.render ). It only reads.

text: Diagram tab (read only): Vertical Metrics Diagram (Metrics) and Nodes Near Zones (Reports). Diagram: one column per master draws the outlines of H, x, b and p against that master's baseline, ascender, cap height, x-height and descender ( FontMetrics(package, master) ; the current master is never switched). One scale fits every master. A sample glyph that is missing, or has no layer in a master, is listed below and left out. Drawing errors stay in the panel. Nodes Near Zones: on-curve nodes that sit within the tolerance (1–30 units, default 4) of a master's baseline, x-height, cap height, ascender or descender but not on it, in the selected glyphs or all glyphs (the default when nothing is selected). Selecting a row shows that glyph and master in the TMetrics preview; "Select glyphs" selects the listed (or the chosen) glyphs in the Font window of the font that was scanned. The tab never writes the font and never opens a history step.

text: Metrics table tab: Master Metrics Table (Font Info). One editable row per master: ascender, descender, x-height and cap height, read as the writer reads them back ( master_values ). An edited cell is validated with the original rule ( validate_metrics : finite 16-bit values, descender ≤ 0 ≤ x-height ≤ cap height ≤ ascender) and listed in the dry run ("Master · field", "Current", "New"). "Set metrics" writes exactly that list through the original route-A writer, metrics.master_writer.write_master_metrics , as one Vertical Metrics: set metrics of <masters> Undo step; it first refuses without the Font window ( require_font_window ) and refuses a value that changed since the preview. Selecting a row shows that master in the TMetrics preview and draws its edited metrics as five labelled guides with a shaded x-height band. The Diagram tab draws every master. The writer changes master metadata only; it never moves glyphs, so a selected composite and its base cannot be shifted twice (Scriptmix TODO:74 is disclosed, and the capHeight write is measured natively in T29).

text: Zones tab: Alignment Zones (Metrics) and Suggest Zones From Overshoots (Guides). Refresh captures every master's zones ( metrics.zones.native.capture ) into one metrics.zones.model.Editor . The zone table shows the staged zones of the chosen master (Kind, Position, Width, Name; double-click to edit); "Add top zone", "Add bottom zone", "Remove selected" and "Suggest from o / O" stage edits as in Alignment Zones, and edits of other masters are kept when you switch. "Suggest from overshoots" measures H, O, x and o (outline geometry, never the cached box, fl#8575) in the current or every master and stages the original suggestions ( suggestions / merge : replace the zone of the same kind at the same position, else the one of the same name, else add; a replaced zone keeps its name, tags and lock), listed with the zone each one replaces. The pending list names every master with a change. "Set zones" writes the staged plan of every changed master through the original route-A writer ( metrics.zones.native , commit_masters ) as ONE Vertical Metrics: set zones of <masters> Undo step. It refuses first when H, O, x or o changed since the overshoot preview, then the writer refuses row errors ( RowRefusal ), a call off the GUI thread or without the Font window, and a font that changed since Refresh. Those refusals leave the font and the stages as they were. Any other failure can leave masters partly written: the tab locks until the app is reopened, as the originals did. The serializer route ( zone_capture / zone_prepare / zone_write_plan ) stays held (fl#8554) and is not used.
